sections.title: Managing with AI: The Innovation Imperative
sections.description: The rise of agentic AI confronts managers with a unique dilemma: To realize the promised exponential increases in productivity, they should give AI agents maximum autonomy. However, this means losing control over agents’ actions, jeopardizing human jobs, and thus exposing their companies and employees to incalculable risks and hardships. This course tackles the dilemma head-on from the perspective of a Wharton undergraduate entering a world in which managing humans, AI agents, and their interactions may become a central leadership challenge. Although AI is being adopted at unprecedented speed, what, when, and how it will disrupt management remain open questions. The course provides frameworks, theories, tools, and experiential learning opportunities that equip students to navigate and adapt their careers to AI-driven change in real time. Innovation and management are the course’s organizing pillars that rapidly coevolve under the impact of AI. After consolidating students’ existing technical AI knowledge and updating it to the state of the art, we will examine how AI reshapes innovation management and practice key innovation tools in their AI-enhanced form. We will then apply these tools to explore emerging AI-enabled innovations across major management domains: Strategy, Marketing, Finance & Accounting, Operations, and HR. Finally, students will use these insights to reenvision their early career paths and design strategies for succeeding in an AI-transformed workplace.
